payload.name: Recreate the whole MacOs tahoe interface as a web app.
payload.description: Recreate the whole MacOs tahoe interface as a web app. Every app and menu should be working

goal.answer: Build a React-based, desktop-only web recreation of the macOS Tahoe interface, including the transparent menu bar, Dock, window manager, Spotlight, Control Center, and eight core apps as visual/interactive mockups with Liquid Glass styling.

payload.plain: Build a React-based, desktop-only web recreation of the macOS Tahoe interface, including the transparent menu bar, Dock, window manager, Spotlight, Control Center, and eight core apps as visual/interactive mockups with Liquid Glass styling.

criteria.answer:
React project scaffolded and runs with `npm run dev` with no build errors.
macOS Tahoe desktop shell renders: transparent menu bar, Dock, desktop wallpaper, and global context menu.
Liquid Glass visual treatment applied to Dock, windows, sidebars, and menus using CSS backdrop-filter and translucent backgrounds.
Window manager supports open, close, minimize, maximize/restore, drag, resize, and z-index ordering for multiple app windows.
Core apps open from Dock/Spotlight and display a visually faithful, mocked UI: Finder, Safari, Notes, System Settings, Calendar, Photos, Phone, Journal.
Spotlight overlay opens via Cmd+Space or menu-bar click and lists apps plus common actions (visual only).
Control Center dropdown opens from menu bar and shows toggles/sliders for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, brightness, volume, etc. (visual only).
All apps use mock/fake data; no backend or real external integrations required.
Target is desktop (1024px+) with mouse/keyboard interaction; mobile responsiveness is out of scope.

constraints.answer: React single-page app; no backend or external API integrations., Desktop-only target (1024px+), mouse and keyboard driven., Liquid Glass effects implemented with CSS backdrop-filter; no WebGL/Canvas simulation., All app content is mock/fake data; no persistence beyond in-memory React state., No mobile or tablet responsive layout; true macOS window model is preserved., No boot/login sequence; app loads straight into the desktop.

plain: React single-page app; no backend or external API integrations.
Desktop-only target (1024px+), mouse and keyboard driven.
Liquid Glass effects implemented with CSS backdrop-filter; no WebGL/Canvas simulation.

phases.answer: Scaffold + Design System + Shell, Window Manager, Dock + App Registry, Liquid Glass UI Primitives, Core Apps Batch 1, Core Apps Batch 2, Spotlight + Control Center + Integration

phaseSnapshots.name: Scaffold + Design System + Shell
phaseSnapshots.goal: Create the React/Vite/TypeScript project, set up global design tokens, and render the static desktop shell.
constraints: Context menu is visual only; real actions wired later.

steps.description: Scaffold project with Vite + React + TypeScript and configure Tailwind CSS.

verification.command: npm install && npm run dev starts without errors and serves a blank page at http://localhost:5173/

steps.description: Create global theme tokens (colors, shadows, radii, spacing) matching Tahoe's light/dark palette.

verification.command: grep -r 'tahoe' src/theme/ returns token definitions

steps.description: Build desktop shell components: Wallpaper, MenuBar, Desktop area, and right-click context menu.

verification.command: MenuBar and Wallpaper render visibly in the browser with no console errors

phaseSnapshots.name: Window Manager
phaseSnapshots.goal: Implement draggable, resizable, focus-managed app windows.
constraints: Minimize animates to Dock in a later phase; for now it collapses to taskbar-like state.

verification.command: A test window renders with title bar buttons visible

steps.description: Add drag and resize interactions with pointer events and bounds checking.

verification.command: User can drag and resize a test window within the viewport

steps.description: Implement window state store (open, minimized, maximized, position, size, z-index focus).

verification.command: Clicking a window brings it to front; z-index updates correctly

phaseSnapshots.name: Dock + App Registry

constraints: Dock uses CSS backdrop-filter Liquid Glass styling.
App icons can be SVG placeholders styled like Tahoe.

steps.description: Create AppRegistry with metadata for the eight core apps plus generic app icon assets.

verification.command: AppRegistry exports an array of eight apps with name, id, icon, and component fields

steps.description: Build Dock component with app icons, hover tooltips, running indicators, and minimized windows area.

verification.command: Dock renders all eight app icons and click opens a window

steps.description: Wire Dock clicks to open/restore windows via the window manager store.

verification.command: Clicking Finder opens a Finder window; clicking again restores focus

phaseSnapshots.name: Liquid Glass UI Primitives
phaseSnapshots.goal: Create reusable Liquid Glass-styled primitives used across apps and overlays.
constraints: No custom shader effects; pure CSS.

steps.description: Implement GlassPanel, GlassButton, GlassSidebar, GlassToolbar, and GlassPopover components with backdrop-filter.

verification.command: Storybook-like demo page shows all primitives with glass effect

steps.description: Add light/dark/tinted variants and a global theme toggle in System Settings scaffold.

verification.command: Toggle switches background theme and glass tint color

steps.description: Add focus/active states and subtle hover transitions.

verification.command: Hover and active states visible on all interactive primitives

phaseSnapshots.name: Core Apps Batch 1

constraints: Apps use Liquid Glass primitives where appropriate.

steps.description: Implement Finder with sidebar, toolbar, path bar, and mocked file grid.

verification.command: Finder window renders sidebar and file icons; folder double-click simulated

steps.description: Implement Safari with address bar, toolbar, tabs, and mocked web page content.

verification.command: Safari window renders address bar and a mocked webpage

steps.description: Implement Notes with note list sidebar and note editor area.

verification.command: Notes window shows list and editor with placeholder text

steps.description: Implement System Settings with settings categories sidebar and detail panes.

verification.command: System Settings window shows categories and a selected pane

phaseSnapshots.name: Core Apps Batch 2
phaseSnapshots.goal: Build visual mockups for Calendar, Photos, Phone, and Journal.

steps.description: Implement Calendar with month grid and event dots.

verification.command: Calendar window renders month view with sample events

steps.description: Implement Photos with grid of placeholder images and single-photo view.

verification.command: Photos window shows image grid and opens a placeholder detail view

steps.description: Implement Phone with Recents, Contacts, and Voicemail tabs.

phaseSnapshots.name: Spotlight + Control Center + Integration
phaseSnapshots.goal: Add global overlays, keyboard shortcuts, and final integration polish.
constraints: Spotlight actions are visual only; no real command execution.
Control Center toggles are visual only.

steps.description: Implement Spotlight overlay with search input, app/action results, and Cmd+Space trigger.

assumptions.answer: Vite + React + TypeScript is acceptable since the user specified React and no stack constraints.; Tailwind CSS is acceptable for styling utility classes.; SVG/PNG icons and static assets are sufficient; no custom icon font generation is needed.; The user will accept a curated set of eight core apps rather than literally every bundled macOS app.; Keyboard shortcuts such as Cmd+Space for Spotlight can use standard browser key handlers without overriding system shortcuts permanently.

charter.intent: Recreate the whole MacOs tahoe interface as a web app. Every app and menu should be working
charter.wowFactor: The page feels like sitting at a real macOS Tahoe desktop, with Liquid Glass windows, a smooth Dock, and recognizable app UIs that respond instantly to clicks and keyboard shortcuts.
charter.confirmedScope: A React desktop-only recreation of the macOS Tahoe shell plus eight core apps (Finder, Safari, Notes, System Settings, Calendar, Photos, Phone, Journal) as visual/interactive mockups. Menus and overlays open and look correct but execute no real actions. Mobile/tablet, backend, and real integrations are out of scope.
charter.demoScript: Open the deployed page and see a Tahoe-style desktop with transparent menu bar and glass Dock. Click Dock icons to open draggable windows for Finder, Safari, Notes, etc. Press Cmd+Space to open Spotlight and search apps. Click the menu-bar Control Center icon to open a glass panel with toggles. Resize, drag, minimize, and close windows.

payload.summary: Phase 1 completed after grader feedback: scaffolded React + TypeScript + Vite project with Tailwind CSS v4; created Tahoe theme tokens, ThemeProvider, and CSS variables; built Wallpaper, MenuBar, Desktop, and ContextMenu shell components. Added Vitest + Testing Library with 14 passing tests covering tokens, ThemeProvider dark-class toggle, MenuBar rendering and click handlers, and ContextMenu escape/edge-clamping behavior. Fixed ContextMenu to clamp to viewport using measured size with fallback defaults for jsdom. Verified with npm run build, npm test, and a headless Chrome screenshot showing the desktop shell.

grade.rationale: All phase requirements are met with concrete evidence: `npm test` passes 14 tests (tokens, ThemeProvider dark-class toggle, MenuBar rendering/clicks, ContextMenu escape and viewport clamping), `npm run build` succeeds with a clean Vite production bundle, and the headless screenshot shows the Tahoe-style desktop with a transparent MenuBar and light-to-pink wallpaper. Code is cleanly scaffolded with React 19 + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind CSS v4, theme tokens are comprehensive, and ContextMenu clamps using measured size with sensible jsdom fallbacks.

payload.summary: Phase 2 — Window Manager completed (retry after grader feedback). Implemented a fully interactive window manager: Window component with Liquid Glass title bar and traffic-light buttons; pointer-event drag/resize with viewport bounds checking and jsdom-safe pointer-capture guards; WindowManagerProvider reducer store supporting open/close/minimize/maximize/restore/focus/move/resize with incremental z-index ordering; WindowManager renderer wiring store state to Window. Added Playwright e2e suite verifying render, focus/z-index, drag, resize, maximize/restore, minimize/close in a real Chromium browser. Captured a sequence of screenshots showing focus, drag, resize, and maximize transitions. Full Vitest (26 tests) and Playwright (6 tests) suites pass; production build succeeds. Source diff archived at /tmp/phase2-window-diff.patch.

grade.rationale: The phase delivers its core goal with real execution evidence: six Playwright e2e tests in Chromium cover render, focus/z-index, drag, resize, maximize/restore, and minimize/close, supported by passing Vitest tests, a successful build, and transition screenshots. Because this was a retry after grader feedback and the source diff is only referenced by an external archive path (not inspectable here), I cannot independently substantiate the implementation quality behind the passing tests, which keeps it from an A.
recommendations: Eliminate the need for retakes by completing all grader-requested verification in the first pass; future phase summaries should not show 'retry after grader feedback.' Evidence: initial submission passes all gates without a retry note.

Make the source diff inspectable in the review artifact rather than only an external archive path, so code-level claims about bounds checking, incremental z-index, and pointer-capture guards can be audited. Evidence: patch content or file links included in the phase output.

Add Playwright coverage for edge cases such as minimum size enforcement, viewport-shrink recovery, and multi-window overlap/focus interactions. Evidence: new e2e tests and screenshots for each edge case.

payload.summary: Phase 3 completed: AppRegistry and Dock are built and wired. The registry maps 8 core apps to icons and placeholder components; Dock renders them with Liquid Glass styling, tooltips, running indicators, and minimized-windows area; clicks open, focus, or restore windows through the window manager store. Unit tests (34 passed) and e2e tests (9 passed) verify the behavior, and the production build succeeds. Evidence includes a git diff patch and a dock screenshot.

grade.rationale: All gates pass; project checks validate. (Phase LLM judge unavailable: empty_response: after 3 attempts)

payload.summary: Phase 4 completed (retry): strengthened the Liquid Glass primitive library and verification. Added real focus/ARIA/state assertions in GlassPrimitives.test.tsx (focus via .focus(), aria-disabled on disabled GlassButton, aria-current on active GlassSidebarItem, computed backdrop-filter inline styles on GlassPanel). Added inline backdrop-filter styles to GlassPanel so the Liquid Glass blur is both testable in jsdom and robust in browser. Added a Playwright e2e integration test (e2e/system-settings.spec.ts) that opens System Settings from the Dock, asserts the glass panel has a blur backdrop-filter, toggles the theme, and captures a screenshot. All 50 unit tests pass; all 11 e2e tests pass; production build succeeds.

grade.rationale: The retry produced solid, behavior-first verification: real focus/ARIA assertions, computed backdrop-filter checks, and a Playwright e2e test that opens System Settings from the Dock, toggles the theme, and asserts the glass blur, backed by passing unit/e2e/build evidence. However, A is precluded because this was a retry, and the runtime proof only covers one app (System Settings) rather than demonstrating the primitives working 'across apps and overlays' as the phase goal states.
recommendations: Integrate and e2e-test the remaining primitives (GlassButton, GlassSidebar, GlassToolbar, GlassPopover) in at least one other app and one overlay surface such as the Dock or Control Center, because the phase goal promises reuse across apps and overlays. Evidence: passing Playwright specs and screenshots for each surface.

Strengthen Liquid Glass visual proof beyond a blur regex by adding visual-regression baselines for light/dark/tinted variants that exercise Tahoe-style layered blur, saturation, and noise, since the current proof only confirms a blur value exists. Evidence: committed baseline screenshots and a Playwright toHaveScreenshot assertion.

Add a browser-level keyboard-navigation e2e test that proves focus, active, aria-disabled, and aria-current behavior with real Tab/Enter/Space input, because jsdom unit assertions do not guarantee actual browser a11y/runtime behavior. Evidence: a passing Playwright spec exercising those states end-to-end.

payload.summary: Phase 5 Core Apps Batch 1 completed. Finder, Safari, Notes, and System Settings are implemented as visual/interactive mockups: Finder with sidebar, toolbar, path bar, and navigable file grid; Safari with address bar, toolbar, tabs, and mocked webpage; Notes with searchable note list sidebar and editor; System Settings with nine-category sidebar and detailed panes (General, Appearance, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Notifications, Sound, Display, Battery, Privacy & Security). Verification: 62 unit tests pass, 12 e2e tests pass, production build succeeds. Added e2e coverage for settings category switching and fixed window-manager scoping to accommodate Safari tabs.

grade.rationale: Verified the four core apps are implemented in src/apps/components.tsx with the expected Finder sidebar/toolbar/path grid, Safari address bar/toolbar/tabs, Notes searchable list/editor, and System Settings nine-category sidebar with all nine panes. Re-ran the agent's verification commands: `npm test` reports 62 passed across 14 files, `npm run test:e2e` reports 12 passed in Chromium (dock, window-manager, and system-settings specs), and `npm run build` completes successfully. The app registry also wires all eight chartered apps, with the remaining four as explicit placeholders for future phases. All self-reported gate verdicts are substantiated by real execution evidence.

payload.summary: Phase 6 Core Apps Batch 2 completed. Calendar, Photos, Phone, and Journal are implemented as visual/interactive mockups: Calendar with month grid, event dots, and calendar sources; Photos with grid of gradient placeholder thumbnails and single-photo detail view; Phone with Recents, Contacts, and Voicemail tabs; Journal with entry list sidebar and editable entry editor. Removed unused AppPlaceholder. Added unit tests for each app (calendar, photos, phone, journal). Verification: 74 unit tests pass, 12 e2e tests pass, production build succeeds.

grade.rationale: All four Core Apps Batch 2 mockups are implemented in src/apps/components.tsx and wired into src/apps/registry.ts. I independently ran the verification commands: `npm test` passed 74/74 unit tests, `npm run test:e2e` passed 12/12 Playwright tests, and `npm run build` produced a production bundle. The new apps (Calendar, Photos, Phone, Journal) are covered by focused unit tests, the AppPlaceholder placeholder was removed, and the Dock e2e test confirms all eight app icons render.

payload.summary: Phase 7 completed after grader feedback. Added three new e2e specs in e2e/global-overlays.spec.ts covering: (1) Spotlight opens via Cmd+Space, filters apps, and opens a window; (2) Control Center opens from the menu bar and shows glass panel, toggles, and sliders; (3) menu-bar app menu and standard menus render mocked dropdowns. Fixed the Spotlight app-selection bug by checking for the app 'category' property instead of the non-existent 'appId'. Extracted contexts/hooks to satisfy oxlint's fast-refresh rules with zero warnings. Final verification: npm run lint 0 warnings/0 errors, npm test 84 unit tests pass, npm run build succeeds, npm run test:e2e 15 tests pass.

grade.rationale: Phase 7 meets its stated goal: Spotlight, Control Center, and menu-bar menus are implemented and verified by real e2e tests (15 passed), plus build, lint (0 warnings/errors), and unit tests (84 passed) all succeeded. However, the summary notes the phase was completed 'after grader feedback,' indicating retries that disqualify an A, and the diff includes unrelated ferment workspace artifacts (.kimchi/, Ferment-GLM5.2/, Ferment-Kimi2.7/) alongside the actual project changes, which creates maintainability noise.
recommendations: Remove or .gitignore ferment workspace artifacts (.kimchi/, Ferment-*/) so the project diff only contains the actual Tahoe web app source; verify with git status and re-run npm run build.

Commit the untracked source/test files (e.g., src/components/shell/Spotlight.tsx, e2e/global-overlays.spec.ts) so the 15 e2e and 84 unit tests are reproducible from a clean checkout; verify with git status and re-run npm test && npm run test:e2e.
Document the grader feedback resolution in the phase notes, specifically what Spotlight bug was fixed and what oxlint fast-refresh changes were made, so retry history is auditable.

payload.finalSummary: Tahoe Web Desktop Shell is complete. Addressed final grader feedback: provided a full code walkthrough (.kimchi/docs/tahoe-walkthrough.md), captured the changed-surface diff (.kimchi/docs/tahoe-diff.txt), updated README.md with explicit mock-only scope boundary, and ran e2e smoke tests against the production preview server. External public deployment was declined by the user, so no remote URL was created. Final verification: npm run lint 0 warnings/0 errors, npm test 84 unit tests pass, npm run build succeeds, npm run test:e2e 15 tests pass against the built production artifact served at http://localhost:4173.

grade.rationale: All seven phases completed, every F-gate and C-gate passed, and the agent supplied command-level evidence that lint, 84 unit tests, 15 e2e tests, and the production build all succeed. However, the review package contains no diff and no independently reachable deployment, screenshot, or screen recording of the rendered Liquid Glass desktop, so the acceptance demo can only be inferred from pass counts rather than directly inspected artifact evidence. That keeps it out of A under the pessimistic standard.
recommendations: Publish a live deployment URL (e.g., Vercel/Netlify/GitHub Pages) or attach representative screenshots/screen recording plus the e2e trace files, so reviewers can verify the rendered Tahoe desktop, app windows, and animations without relying solely on terminal pass counts.

Attach the full changed-surface diff content to the review package and confirm no placeholder stubs, dead code, test-only artifacts, or unwired production paths remain; the council cannot inspect source structure from pass counts alone.

Expose the e2e test report and coverage output as artifacts, mapping each acceptance-demo step (drag, resize, minimize, maximize, Cmd+Space Spotlight, Control Center toggle) to a specific passing test case, so the evidence is substantiated rather than summarized.
